newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem to Fujimori: "I would have done the same".
newsitem.headline: Menem to Fujimori: "I would have done the same".

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem on Wednesday praised the "spectacular courage" of President Alberto Fujimori who sent troops in to end Peru's hostage crisis and said he would have done the same thing.

"He waited, he opened talks, international organisations ... intervened. But faced with the 'firmness' of the terrorists, he took the decision we all know of, which was very valiant and showed spectacular courage," he said.

"I would have acted in the same way, the same manner -- wait, talk, and when the right moment comes, when there's no more time left, strike," Menem, who is one of Fujimori's closest allies in Latin America, told local radio.

However, he qualified his praise of the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence where Marxist rebels were holding 72 hostages, pointing out that one hostage, two commandos and all 14 guerrillas died. "It was a partial success because there were deaths," he said, blaming them on the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
Hen also hinted Fujimori may have taken too many chances, saying: "Everything went fine. Everybody is applauding. If things had gone bad they would have called him irresponsible."
Fujimori has also described the hostage rescue as a "qualified" success because of the losses incurred.
